title: Leonurus japonicus Houtt. modulates neuronal apoptosis in intracerebral hemorrhage: Insights from network pharmacology and molecular docking.
authors: Wu, Jia-Wei; Gao, Wei; Shen, Li-Ping; Chen, Yong-Lin; Du, Shi-Qing; Du, Zhi-Yong; Zhao, Xu-Dong; Lu, Xiao-Jie
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究中药益母草对脑出血后神经元凋亡的调控，分子对接仅针对JAK蛋白与小分子，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关系微弱。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Leonurus japonicus Houtt. (Labiatae), commonly known as Chinese motherwort, is a herbaceous flowering plant that is native to Asia. It is widely acknowledged in traditional medicine for its diuretic, hypoglycemic, antiepileptic properties and neuroprotection. Currently, Leonurus japonicus (Leo) is included in the Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) recognizes Leo for its myriad pharmacological attributes, but its efficacy against ICH-induced neuronal apoptosis is unclear. AIMS OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to identify the potential targets and regulatory mechanisms of Leo in alleviating neuronal apoptosis after ICH. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study employed network pharmacology, UPLC-Q-TOF-MS technique, molecular docking, pharmacodynamic studies, western blotting, and immunofluorescence techniques to explore its potential mechanisms. RESULTS: Leo was found to assist hematoma absorption, thus improving the neurological outlook in an ICH mouse model. Importantly, molecular docking highlighted JAK as Leo's potential therapeutic target in ICH scenarios. Further experimental evidence demonstrated that Leo adjusts JAK1 and STAT1 phosphorylation, curbing Bax while augmenting Bcl-2 expression. CONCLUSION: Leo showcases potential in mitigating neuronal apoptosis post-ICH, predominantly via the JAK/STAT mechanism.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：Leonurus japonicus Houtt.（唇形科），俗称益母草，是一种原产于亚洲的草本开花植物。在传统医学中，它因其利尿、降血糖、抗癫痫特性和神经保护作用而被广泛认可。目前，Leonurus japonicus（Leo）已被收录于《中华人民共和国药典》。传统中医（TCM）认可Leo的多种药理属性，但其对脑出血（ICH）诱导的神经元凋亡的疗效尚不明确。研究目的：本研究旨在确定Leo在减轻ICH后神经元凋亡中的潜在靶点和调控机制。材料与方法：本研究采用网络药理学、UPLC-Q-TOF-MS技术、分子对接、药效学研究、蛋白质印迹法和免疫荧光技术来探索其潜在机制。结果：研究发现Leo有助于血肿吸收，从而改善ICH小鼠模型中的神经学预后。重要的是，分子对接突出显示JAK是Leo在ICH情境下的潜在治疗靶点。进一步的实验证据表明，Leo调节JAK1和STAT1磷酸化，抑制Bax同时增强Bcl-2表达。结论：Leo在减轻ICH后神经元凋亡方面展现出潜力，主要通过JAK/STAT机制发挥作用。
